content.user_title: Build and Verify iOS Apps in Simulator
content.value_statement: A successful iOS build does not prove tests pass or screens display correctly. This skill guides Simulator testing, visual checks, and evidence collection for review.
actual_capabilities: Check macOS, Xcode, and available Simulator runtimes before starting.
Discover projects, workspaces, schemes, and Simulator destinations.
Build the selected scheme with local derived data and inspect compiler diagnostics.
Run targeted tests and full suites, then extract test summaries with xcresulttool.
Install and launch a Simulator app, capture screenshots, and collect process crash logs.
Prepare review evidence covering environment details, build results, test totals, screenshots, and verification gaps.
limitations: Requires a Mac with Xcode and suitable Simulator runtimes already installed.
Example commands require project-specific workspace, scheme, and Simulator values.
Simulator verification does not establish physical-device behavior or App Store readiness.
Screenshots require visual inspection; the workflow does not supply automated visual comparisons.

use_cases.title: Verify an iOS feature change
use_cases.description: Build an updated app, test affected behavior, and capture changed screens before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Investigate a Simulator failure
use_cases.description: Reproduce a failing test or app crash and collect assertion messages, process logs, and screenshots.

use_cases.title: Review verification evidence
use_cases.description: Collect the exact scheme, toolchain, Simulator details, test totals, and visual evidence needed to assess a proposed change.

prompt_templates.title: Check the development environment
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this Mac for Xcode and available iOS Simulator runtimes. Report missing prerequisites without installing anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: confirm the machine can run the workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Build a selected app
prompt_templates.prompt: Find this repository's workspace and app schemes. Ask me about ambiguous schemes, then build the selected scheme on an available Simulator.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: establish a reproducible build destination.

prompt_templates.title: Test and inspect changed screens
prompt_templates.prompt: Run tests affected by my changes, then the full suite. Launch the app and capture each changed screen. Report failures and verification gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine automated testing with visual evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a crash and prepare review evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Reproduce the reported crash on a selected Simulator. Collect process logs and screenshots, run relevant tests, and prepare review evidence. Avoid erasing shared devices.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: investigate failures while preserving shared development resources.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: summarize verification after building, testing, and checking the updated screen.
output: Environment: selected app scheme, Simulator model, iOS runtime, and Xcode version recorded.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: report what prevents verification when Xcode is unavailable.
output: Verification stopped because xcodebuild is unavailable.
No build, tests, app launch, or screenshots were completed.
Xcode was not installed or modified.

best_practices: Use trusted repositories and confirm the scheme and Simulator UDID before building or changing app state.
Preserve xcodebuild failure status when piping logs, and inspect current test results rather than inferring success from output alone.
Run affected tests before the full suite, inspect changed screens, and exclude generated .build artifacts from commits.
anti_patterns: Treating a successful build as proof that tests pass or screens look correct.
Guessing an ambiguous scheme or choosing a Simulator only by its display name.
Erasing a shared Simulator or launching duplicate builds of the same scheme.

faq.question: Does this skill install Xcode?
faq.answer: No. It stops and reports the missing prerequisite when xcodebuild is unavailable.

faq.question: Can I use a hosted Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow supports local and hosted Macs with Xcode installed, including Macswarm Pods.

faq.question: Is XcodeBuildMCP required?
faq.answer: No. Shell commands are provided. A connected XcodeBuildMCP server can supply equivalent build, test, launch, and screenshot tools.

faq.question: How does it choose a scheme and Simulator?
faq.answer: It consults repository guidance, asks about ambiguous app schemes, and selects a Simulator by UDID, preferably one already booted.

faq.question: Where are test results and screenshots stored?
faq.answer: Examples store test results in .build/Results.xcresult and screenshots in .build/screens. Generated .build content should not be committed.

faq.question: Does a passing test suite prove the interface is correct?
faq.answer: No. The workflow also requires screenshots and visual inspection of changed screens, with any remaining verification gaps stated explicitly.
